Title: Liver Regeneration — Part 1
Content: The human liver is capable of regenerating large amounts of its tissue mass after disease, injury, or surgery. The regeneration process replaces all the specialized cell types necessary for the liver to carry out vital functions.

Scientists studied the process that produces the specialized cells of the liver during development to help them understand how the liver regenerates. Figure `1` shows part of the development process of specialized liver cells from pluripotent stem cells. Pluripotent stem cells have the capacity to develop into all of the body cell types. Multipotent stem cells can develop into a limited number of cell types.
